## How do I bring in my bank transactions?

<a id="import-bank-statement"></a>

Import the statement file your bank gives you: PDF, a scan or phone photo, Excel, CSV, OFX or QBO. There is no bank login. Every row is checked against the statement’s balances before it is brought in.

**Where:** **Banking › Bank Feeds** (`/bank-feeds`)

1. Open Bank Feeds / Import and choose "Import a statement file", or drop the file onto the window. In the menu: File > Import Bank File…. → **Banking › Bank Feeds** (`/bank-feeds`)
2. Choose the bank or credit card account the statement belongs to and check the rows that were read.
3. Import, then review each line. → **Banking › Review bank transactions** (`/bank-review`)

> Good to know: Ironbooks never connects to your bank. You download the statement from the bank’s website and import the file.
>
> Good to know: No file? Type the transactions into the account’s register, or paste them into Enter many transactions.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I bring in my bank transactions?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I categorize the bank lines I imported?

<a id="review-bank-transactions"></a>

Review bank transactions shows each imported line with a suggested match or account. You confirm, change or exclude it.

**Where:** **Banking › Review bank transactions** (`/bank-review`)

1. Open Review bank transactions and pick the Bank Account. → **Banking › Review bank transactions** (`/bank-review`)
2. For each line under To Review: "Confirm Match" when it matches something you already entered, or "Use suggestion" to add it to the suggested account. Pick another account if the suggestion is wrong.
3. Not sure about a line? "Ask AI" asks your connected model to pick an account. You still confirm.
4. "Apply Rules" runs your bank rules; "Auto-add Suggested" adds every line whose suggestion is sure enough.
5. A line that is not yours, or a duplicate: Exclude it.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I categorize the bank lines I imported?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I make bank lines categorize themselves?

<a id="bank-rules"></a>

A bank rule tells Ironbooks which account to use for bank lines that look alike, such as every SHELL OIL charge going to Fuel. It also offers a rule when you repeat a choice.

**Where:** **Banking › Bank rules** (`/bank-rules`)

1. Open Bank rules and click "New rule". → **Banking › Bank rules** (`/bank-rules`)
2. Under "When a bank line…", say what the description contains. Under "Then put it in…", choose the account.
3. Click "Test on recent lines" to see what it would catch, choose Suggest or Add automatically, then "Save rule".
4. Under "Rules we can make for you", accept the rules Ironbooks offers from choices you repeated.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I make bank lines categorize themselves?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I reconcile a bank or credit card account?

<a id="reconcile-monthly"></a>

Reconciling checks your books against the statement, so you know every transaction is right. Do it when each statement arrives.

**Where:** **Banking › Reconcile** (`/reconcile`)

1. Open Reconcile, choose the account, and enter the Statement Date and Statement Ending Balance. Click "Start Reconciliation". → **Banking › Reconcile** (`/reconcile`)
2. Tick each transaction that appears on the statement ("Mark All" ticks everything). Enter any service charge or interest when asked.
3. When Difference is 0.00, click "Finish Reconciliation".
4. Something missing? Add it, or import the statement, then come back: an unfinished reconciliation can be resumed. → **Banking › Bank Feeds** (`/bank-feeds`)

> Good to know: A small difference you cannot find can be closed with "Finish with Adjustment".
>
> Good to know: Past reconciliations and their reports are under Reconciliation History on the same screen.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I reconcile a bank or credit card account?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I undo or redo a reconciliation?

<a id="undo-reconciliation"></a>

Undo Last Reconciliation un-ticks the latest reconciliation for an account, so you can do it again.

**Where:** **Banking › Reconcile** (`/reconcile`)

1. Open Reconcile and choose the account. → **Banking › Reconcile** (`/reconcile`)
2. Click "Undo Last Reconciliation" and confirm. Repeat to go back further, one statement at a time.
3. The Reconciliation Discrepancy report shows reconciled transactions that were changed afterwards.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I undo or redo a reconciliation?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I record a bank deposit?

<a id="make-deposit"></a>

Make Deposits groups the customer payments you took to the bank into one deposit, so it matches your bank statement.

**Where:** **Banking › Make Deposits** (`/deposits?new=1`)

1. Open Make Deposits. → **Banking › Make Deposits** (`/deposits?new=1`)
2. Choose the bank account under "Deposit To" and tick the payments you deposited under "Payments in Undeposited Funds".
3. Other money in (a loan, an owner contribution): "Add Line" with the account it belongs to. Kept some cash? Tick "Take cash back from this deposit".
4. Click "Make Deposit".

> Good to know: Payments wait in Undeposited Funds until they are put on a deposit.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I record a bank deposit?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I move money between my own accounts?

<a id="transfer-funds"></a>

Transfer Funds moves money between your own accounts, for example checking to savings.

**Where:** **Banking › Transfer Funds** (`/transfers`)

1. Open Transfer Funds and click "New Transfer". → **Banking › Transfer Funds** (`/transfers`)
2. Pick the From Account and the To Account, the amount and the date, then save.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I move money between my own accounts?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I add a bank or credit card account?

<a id="add-bank-account"></a>

Bank accounts lists your bank and credit card accounts with their balances. Each one is also an account in the Chart of Accounts.

**Where:** **Banking › Bank accounts** (`/banking`)

1. Open Bank accounts and add a new account. → **Banking › Bank accounts** (`/banking`)
2. Choose the right type: a checking or savings account is a Bank account, a card is a Credit Card account.
3. Enter its balance on your start date in the Setup Interview, or import its history. → **Setup › Setup Interview** (`/onboarding`)

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I add a bank or credit card account?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I see or type transactions in a register?

<a id="use-register"></a>

A register shows every transaction in one account, like a checkbook, with a running balance. You can type new rows straight into it.

**Where:** **Banking › Registers** (`/registers`)

1. Open Registers and pick an account (Ctrl+R). → **Banking › Registers** (`/registers`)
2. Type a row and press Enter. It saves as the right check, deposit, transfer, card charge or journal entry.
3. A new payee asks whether it is a Customer, Vendor, Employee or Other, right there.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I see or type transactions in a register?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I enter or paste many transactions at once?

<a id="batch-enter"></a>

Enter many transactions is a spreadsheet-style grid for checks, deposits, card charges, bills, invoices or journal entries. Each row is checked as you go and saved as its own transaction.

**Where:** **Banking › Enter many transactions** (`/accountant/batch-enter`)

1. Open Enter many transactions and pick the transaction type. → **Banking › Enter many transactions** (`/accountant/batch-enter`)
2. Type rows, or paste them from Excel or Google Sheets.
3. Fix the rows marked red, then save.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I enter or paste many transactions at once?", or ask Ask AI.*

## How do I track a loan and its payments?

<a id="track-loan"></a>

Loans tracks what you owe, each payment and how much of it is interest. "What if" compares another rate, payment or term.

**Where:** **Banking › Loans** (`/loans`)

1. Open Loans and click "Add a Loan". Enter its amount, rate and term. Tick "already being paid" if you have been paying it. → **Banking › Loans** (`/loans`)
2. Set up each payment. Ironbooks splits it between principal and interest.

*In the app: Help & Glossary → "How do I track a loan and its payments?", or ask Ask AI.*
